text:
carla: Heads-up — saw a 3x jump in Dedicated GPU spend for us-west-2 starting ~02:10 UTC and autoscaler spun up ~18 extra nodes. Investigating, but cluster health checks were flapping when nodes came up.
ben: Ack. Any logs from the healthcheck proxies?
carla: Logs show repeated 502/timeout from healthcheck-proxy (sidecar) to kubelet. Suspect something network-level is dropping TCP probes.
alice: I just checked firewall audit logs — around 02:08 a policy change landed from a security rollout job (PR #6421). It tightened an inspection ACL for the mgmt-subnet and started blocking ephemeral ports used by health checks.
ops-bot: deploybot:policy-update applied by @security-team (rollout/acl-tighten) 
ben: That would explain flapping. Autoscaler saw failures -> marked nodes NotReady -> replaced -> rinse/repeat. Cost loop.
dave: Can we hotfix by adding a narrow allow-rule for k8s health ports (10250, 10255) between mgmt-subnet and worker-subnet?
security-team: We intentionally blocked broad ephemeral ranges; didn't intend kubelet probes to be affected. Was expecting them on different ALB path. Sorry — we missed the stateful sidecars port mapping.
carla: Temporary mitigation: I'm going to add a temporary allow rule for tcp:10250 from mgmt->workers and open 30000-32767 for nodePort health checks for the duration. Will monitor.
alice: If you add that, we should also pause autoscaler policies to avoid further churn. ben, can you scale down aggressive policy?
ben: Scaling policy to conservative in 2m. Command I ran: `kubectl annotate hpa/autoscaler team=conservative --overwrite` (not perfect but stops the burst).
dave: Added temporary allow-rule (rule-id rl-tnp-834). Pushed to firewall staging and then to prod.
ops-bot: firewall:rule-apply success rl-tnp-834 -> prod by dave at 02:22 UTC
carla: After rule applied, node flapping subsided. New nodes stabilized and pods are healthy. Cost alarms still firing — billing lag.
security-team: We're rolling back the overly broad ACL change and will open a scoped exception for kubelet/health traffic. Creating PR to revert and add explicit exceptions. PR #6426.
alice: Please attach the runbook link and add postmortem notes to the incident tracker. Need an RCA: why the policy rollout didn't catch the k8s dependency matrix.
carla: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/k8s-health-firewall.md — section 2 has the quick checklist I followed.
ben: Billing team: can you mute the cost alert while we reconcile? It keeps paging on noise.
ops-bot: alert-manager:muted alert/gpu-cost-spike for 6h by carla
dave: Action items: (1) security-team to revert/or refine ACL (PR #6426) — owner: security-team — ETA 4h, (2) infra to add automated integration test that simulates kubelet health traffic against new ACLs — owner: ben — ETA 1w, (3) update rollout playbook to include k8s port matrix — owner: alice — ETA 2d, (4) runbook link updated with firewall checklist — owner: carla — ETA 1h.
security-team: Agreed. We'll also add a guard in the rollout pipeline that runs the ACL simulator.
carla: Temporary cost hit estimated ~$4200 extra for the burst window. Will include in incident cost summary.
dave: Will follow up with a small infra config diff to ensure nodePort ranges are explicitly allowed by default in mgmt ACL.
alice: Thanks team. Once PR #6426 merges, remind me and I'll run the postmortem template.
carla: Closing for now — cluster stable and autoscaler paused on conservative. Reopen thread if we see new flapping. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Deployment notice — PR #6426 (acl revert + exception) queued for canary at 06:00 UTC
carla: tagging ops slack channel and incident tracker: #incident-2005-gpu-firewall-cost (created)
ben: thx all, lesson: any firewall change -> run the k8s-health smoke tests in staging before prod rollouts.
